questions.prompt: Why does the $SI / $FN split make timestomping detectable?
options: Both attributes are read-only and cannot be changed
$SI is settable through the Windows API via SetFileTime while $FN is maintained by the kernel and not reachable that way, so backdating $SI leaves $FN inconsistent
The two attributes are stored on different volumes
questions.explanation: A timestomping tool can reach $STANDARD_INFORMATION but not $FILE_NAME, so a $SI Born earlier than its own $FN Born is structurally impossible without manipulation.

questions.prompt: Why is $SI Modified earlier than $FN Born frequently a false positive?
options: Copying a file creates a new $FN with current timestamps while $SI Modified is inherited from the source -- normal behavior that MFTECmd flags separately as Copied
$FN Born is never populated on copied files
questions.explanation: Copy inheritance is the single most common false positive in timestomping analysis, which is why MFTECmd separates the Copied indicator from the SI<FN one.

questions.prompt: What does uSecZeros indicate in MFTECmd output?
options: The file has no timestamps at all
Timestamps with zeroed sub-second components, common when a tool sets times with second-granularity input on a system where other files show noisy precision
The file is zero bytes in size
The MFT record has been zeroed out
questions.explanation: Windows records 100-nanosecond precision naturally. Exact zeros across all four values stand out against surrounding files and suggest programmatic timestamp setting.

questions.prompt: Why is the $SI Accessed timestamp unreliable on most modern Windows systems?
options: It was removed entirely in Windows 10
NtfsDisableLastAccessUpdate has four states since Windows 10 v1803, and system-managed mode disables last-access updates on larger volumes around a 128 GB threshold
It is overwritten every time the file is modified
questions.explanation: On most modern systems last-access updates are simply not maintained, so a stale or absent Accessed time is a configuration artifact rather than evidence about user behavior.
